previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for bright red blood per rectum and new bruising, with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and prior venous thromboembolism on Lovenox. Initial evaluation revealed anemia with a hemoglobin of 10.0 g/dL, which dropped to 26.8% hematocrit, prompting a transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells with good response. The bleeding was attributed to Lovenox use, with hemorrhoids identified as the likely source during colonoscopy, along with a non-bleeding gastric ulcer and gastritis on EGD. Lovenox was held and later restarted at a reduced dose of 60 mg daily. Hyperglycemia was noted on admission with a glucose of 381 mg/dL and HbA1c of 8.5%, consistent with steroid-induced diabetes. She remained stable, with improvement in hemoglobin and glucose levels, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up arranged.
problems: Chronic myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified
Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
